sources.title: Frink README
sources.locator: Features; Supported Agents; Install; Linux; Also in the box
sources.finding: Desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Cursor side by side (up to four panes, worktrees), Flows with triggers (Linear, Jira, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog, Vercel, webhook, schedule), a Work Queue, permissions gate, plugins and MCP, own AI sign-in, local SQLite; macOS 13+ and Linux builds, iPhone beta; MIT; official builds send anonymous usage counts and crash reports.

sources.title: Getting started
sources.locator: First launch; Connect an AI account; Start your first chat
sources.finding: Connect an existing Claude, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot or Cursor login, then start a general or project chat; the matching CLI must be installed and logged in.

sources.title: AI accounts
sources.locator: macOS and Linux for now; one sign-in per provider per machine; bundled claude binary
sources.finding: Frink stores no Claude or Codex token and runs the signed-in account; OpenCode, Copilot and Cursor are macOS and Linux only; Windows is not supported yet; Frink ships its own bundled claude binary.

sources.title: Task lifecycle
sources.locator: Task states; Agent-declared states; Stopping a task; Renderer-only recovery
sources.finding: Task states Pending, Running, Plan Ready, Needs Attention, Ready for review, Completed, Failed, Cancelled and Interrupted; agent completion signals; a question waits about 9.5 minutes; macOS keeps a running task alive after the window closes but quitting stops it.

sources.title: Flows
sources.locator: Anatomy of a flow; Project defaults; Flow briefing; Run history
sources.finding: Visual pipelines with one trigger (manual, webhook, schedule, post-task) plus blocks, run history, flow briefing and custom nodes; Flow steps run on Claude or OpenAI only; agents can patch flows through MCP tools.

sources.title: Plugins
sources.locator: Two kinds of plugin; Letting a service tell Frink when something happens; Run your own relay
sources.finding: Plugins provide chat tools and Flow triggers/actions; events arrive only while Frink is open and online, best effort and not queued; relay is Frink's address or your own via FRINK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL.

sources.title: MCP servers
sources.locator: Where Frink stores MCPs; Credentials: per-machine; Security considerations
sources.finding: Frink is an MCP client with auto-import of servers, per-project or global servers and per-machine encrypted credentials.

sources.title: Permissions
sources.locator: The short version; The three scopes; What's always blocked; Auto permission mode
sources.finding: Per-tool permission prompts with project, user and managed policy scopes, an always-blocked credential-path list that is a static check not a sandbox, and an Auto mode.

sources.title: What Frink sends
sources.locator: Usage counts; Turning usage counts off; Crash reports
sources.finding: Official builds send anonymous usage counts to PostHog (switch off in Settings, Privacy) and crash reports to Sentry (not switchable); source builds send nothing; update check contacts Frink's download server.

sources.title: Worktree setup
sources.locator: Two different .frink paths; Configuring setup commands
sources.finding: Chats can run in a git worktree under ~/.frink/worktrees with per-project setup commands from .frink/worktrees.json.

sources.title: Projects and general chat
sources.finding: A chat has a project folder or is a general chat with no files; projects can be started from scratch, opened or cloned.

sources.title: Reviewing changes
sources.finding: Every changed file shows as a diff; the built-in editor and terminal allow fixes; chats can roll back to a checkpoint.

sources.title: Frink relay
sources.locator: What it is not; The two secrets
sources.finding: Small relay that forwards webhook and phone traffic to the desktop app without storing anything; deliveries are dropped when the app is not connected; relay learns the subscribe key.

sources.title: Frink for iPhone
sources.locator: Connect your computer; Use and recovery; Alerts
sources.finding: Native iPhone companion (TestFlight beta): pair by QR through the relay, Queue, Flows, History and starting chats; execution and files stay on the computer, which must stay awake with Frink open.

sources.title: MIT License
sources.finding: MIT License, copyright Benji Norval, covering the repository.

sources.title: Frink package manifest
sources.finding: Version 0.4.0, MIT; dependencies include the Claude Agent SDK, @sentry/electron, posthog-node, croner and Electron tooling; no bin entry, so no CLI.

sources.title: Flow admission config
sources.finding: Flow runs are admitted up to a configurable maxConcurrentRuns with queuing.

sources.title: Admission store
sources.finding: Computes free slots from maxConcurrentRuns minus occupied runs; excess runs queue.

sources.title: Schedule trigger
sources.finding: Flow schedule triggers use croner cron expressions inside the desktop app.

sources.title: Webhook listener
sources.finding: Desktop webhook listener verifies signatures and starts flows from relayed deliveries.

sources.title: Worktree creation
sources.locator: git worktree add under git lock (L118, L144)
sources.finding: Creates a worktree after fetching the base, serialized per project with a git lock.

sources.title: Flows MCP tools
sources.finding: Frink exposes frink_flows_* MCP tools so agents can list, read, patch and run flows inside Frink.

sources.title: Analytics client
sources.finding: Sends PostHog events including pr_created, gated by the Share Usage Analytics setting.

sources.title: Privacy switch
sources.finding: Settings tab holds the Share Usage Analytics switch.

sources.title: GitHub repository API
sources.finding: Public repository benord-labs/frink: 177 stars, MIT license, pushed 2026-11-17 (observed 2026-11-17).

sources.title: Frink 0.4.0 release
sources.finding: Release 0.4.0 published 2026-10-16 with macOS arm64/x64 DMGs, Linux x64/arm64 AppImages and arm64/amd64 debs.

sources.title: Bounded search: other clients
sources.locator: ls src mobile relay; package.json bin; grep -rniE "android|express.*listen|vscode extension" src mobile/app.json
sources.finding: Only the Electron app, an iPhone app (Android only appears as an audio-permission flag) and the relay exist; package.json has no bin so there is no CLI; no web client or editor extension.

sources.title: Bounded search: cost and billing
sources.finding: Cost fields exist only in Claude message types and context-usage code; no per-task cost UI, budget or spend limit.

sources.title: Bounded search: teams, roles, SSO
sources.finding: No user accounts, organizations, roles, SSO or presence; the managed policy file is the only admin construct.

sources.title: Bounded search: remote execution
sources.finding: ssh and remote matches are git, shell env and MCP transport handling; no remote host, container or VM execution.

sources.title: Bounded search: specs and memory
sources.finding: No persistent product spec or memory store; Flow briefing is shared text per flow.

sources.title: Bounded search: dependencies and limits
sources.finding: No task dependencies, token or spend limits; flows have edges and admission limits.
